vla_action_adapter.Why can a VLA's raw output not be sent s: Walk the raw output space: normalized, padded to a shared model width, possibly delta, gripper in a dataset convention. Map each adapter step to which of those it undoes and what goes wrong if it is skipped.
vla_action_adapter.What does a delta mask such as make_bool: Expand the positive and negative counts into a per-dim boolean list. Cover which dims get the state added, why joints suit deltas, and why an open/close gripper command is naturally absolute.
vla_action_adapter.In a chunk of H delta actions, is each s: Compare adding one state to all H steps against a running sum over steps. Cover which reference state openpi uses and what the unsqueeze at dim -2 does for batched chunks.
vla_action_adapter.What does np.sign return for a gripper v: Evaluate both orders on exactly 0.5 and on values in (0, 0.5). Cover sign(0) = 0, what a zero gripper command means to the env, and why the raw [0, 1] value carries no sign information.
vla_action_adapter.Does it matter whether the gripper is fl: Use the odd symmetry of sign. Cover sign(-g) versus -sign(g), including g = 0, and contrast it with a step that would not commute, such as a threshold that maps 0 to +1.
vla_action_adapter.Binarized versus continuous gripper comm: Weigh a smaller effective action space against grasp precision. Cover how a binary gripper affects sampling and exploration, and when partial closing or force control needs continuous values.
vla_action_adapter.Quantile (q01/q99) versus z-score normal: Compare how one outlier moves the mean/std versus the 1st/99th percentiles, and what each openpi inverse does to padded dims (pass-through versus padding stats of mean 0, std 1). Note which model types use which.
